svg.font-family: 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Liberation Mono', monospace
svg.text: dnswhy doctor
warn
Scope "corp.internal" points at an unreachable nameserver: 198.51.100.53
Every name under corp.internal fails after a 5s wait, instead of falling
back to the default nameservers.
That is how a disconnected VPN or a stopped container makes one domain,
and only that domain, stop working.
note
/etc/resolver/search.only adds a search domain and nothing else
It appends corp.internal to single-label names; it cannot answer
anything itself.
warn
/etc/resolver/stale.example is not in the live configuration
scutil --dns shows no resolver for "stale.example", so the file is being
ignored.
macOS reads this directory when it changes; a file written as root with
odd permissions, or a domain that another scope already claims, can end
up ignored.
warn
/etc/resolver/typo.example has lines macOS does not understand
nameserver198.51.100.77
Only nameserver, domain, search, port, timeout and search_order are
read.
Nothing else in the file is usable, so it has no effect at all.
note
Search domains in use: corp.internal
A name with no dot is also tried as name.corp.internal.
This is why a bare word can resolve to a host you did not mean.
warn
doubled.example has more than one IPv4 address in /etc/hosts
line 8, line 9.
The first entry wins; the rest are dead weight.
note
pinned.corp.internal in /etc/hosts shadows the "corp.internal" scope
resolver #3 will never be asked for this name.
1 in order, 3 worth knowing, 4 worth fixing
